dossier.public_summary: This is a short 1.05-day flat-bottomed dip seen 673 times on a small 3335 K M dwarf, squarely on the target with no even/odd difference or secondary eclipse. The star itself spins at the same period with strong spot modulation, which explains the large outside-dip swing and the large measured depth changes, but does not make the flat-bottom shape. The best explanation remains a ~2.7 Earth-radius planet; the depth scatter is likely spot/activity systematics and needs simultaneous ground-based photometry and spectroscopy to confirm.

reasons.why: Strongly flat-bottomed transit favours planet over V grazing binary.
Planet-sized radius and low undiluted depth 6125 ppm, not stellar eclipse.
Difference imaging puts dip on target with closest plausible neighbours >20 sigma away, against off-target EB.
No odd/even depth difference and secondary snr -15.75 with depth_over_dip -0.1247, no EB secondary.
Large phase modulation is present but identical in morphology to stellar spot modulation, not inconsistent with unocculted spots on 1.05 d rotating M dwarf; flat-bottom and on-target outweigh it.
Period equals rotation period (1.05482 d vs rotation 1.055 d) but with flat shape and RUWE 1.133 no binary signs, signal is not spot shape.
